audit.whatIsWrong: Every lane-difficulty line frames the matchup around 'tracking Scrap Shield', but Scrap Shield is a flat 6-second cooldown — it is never down long enough to be a window.
audit.why: Rumble's kit file gives W a cd of 6 at all ranks. The real resource is Heat: at 100% he Overheats and cannot cast at all.
audit.corrected: Difficulty re-anchored on the Heat bar and Overheat lockout instead of Scrap Shield; tldr, winCon and breakdown.cooldowns rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] said Sett's Show Stopper makes level 6 his window, while win[4]/whys[4] and the packet chart say Rumble's Equalizer spikes the fight for him.
audit.why: The Equalizer is a 1750-range zone on a 130/105/80s cooldown that cuts Sett's only engage line; Sett's R is 400 range.
audit.corrected: Level 6 given to Rumble in both layers with the Equalizer cooldown stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction — Overheat leaving Rumble unable to cast, so Facebreaker (E, 16s at rank 1) into a cashed Haymaker lands uncontested — was never stated as the commit trigger.
audit.why: Rumble's passive locks out all spellcasting during Overheat; that is the only stretch where Scrap Shield cannot answer Sett's engage.
audit.corrected: Stated in tldr, winCon, breakdown.cooldowns and wants.you[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Scrap Shield was labelled 'matchup-defining' in the cooldown breakdown.
audit.why: 6s flat. Flamespitter at 10s rank 1 and Equalizer at 130s rank 1 are the punishable cooldowns.

edits.before: His DoT chunks you — build MR, bait his shield, all-in on his Q cooldown. Sett wins by trading around Rumble's Scrap Shield and cashing the pattern: build MR, bait his heat, all-in.
edits.after: His DoT chunks you — build MR, bait his Heat, all-in when he Overheats. Sett wins by trading around Rumble's Heat bar, not his 6s Scrap Shield: build MR, E-stun in, cash the grit.

edits.before: Build MR, bait his heat, all-in. Track Scrap Shield before every commit and keep the wave on your side.
edits.after: Build MR, bait his Heat, all-in. Scrap Shield is only 6s — commit when he Overheats, not when it is down.

edits.before: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — Bait it, then commit. Track it before every engage. - Rumble The Equalizer: A long line of fire that zones and chunks — his teamfight tool. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Rumble Flamespitter: 10s at rank 1, and Overheat locks his casts — that is your commit window. - Rumble The Equalizer: A long line of fire that zones and chunks — his teamfight tool. Dodge or sidestep it.

edits.before: The Show Stopper online — you can start fights Rumble doesn't want. Suplex him into your wave or tower, never into his own minions.
edits.after: The Equalizer out-spikes your R at 6: 130s of zone that cuts your engage line. Suplex him out of the flames, not through them.

edits.before: Engage when his Q heat is high or overheated
edits.after: Engage the moment he Overheats and cannot cast

notes: Chart was wholly inverted against a 54.85% Sett win rate and against its own whys text (whys[1..3],[5],[6] all describe Sett winning). Rebuilt to the packet chart. Rumble's Scrap Shield is a 6s cooldown and cannot be 'tracked' as an engage window — that framing is spread across many Rumble matchups repo-wide and deserves a global sweep, same as the mirror's note about 'Flamespitter channel gets interrupted' (Flamespitter has no channel flag).
